clue.text: Fat boys at international guzzle bubbly entertaining redhead

indicators.note: to guzzle is to take in greedily, so the first pair of pieces swallows the rest

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: entertaining a guest means holding them inside, so the champagne goes round the red top

parts.note: Moet is a champagne house, and bubbly is slang for champagne
the head, or first letter, of red is R

explanation.surface: Portly lads at an international gathering knock back champagne with a ginger-haired companion.
explanation.definitionFit: Amoretti are chubby infant cupids in Renaissance art, so plump little boys is a playful description.

clue.text: Striker somewhat misconstrues opportunity in recession

indicators.note: receding means going backwards, so the run of letters is read right to left
somewhat means only part of the following words is used, a run of letters inside them

explanation.surface: A footballer slightly misreads a scoring chance as the team falls back.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who strikes a pose is an affected show-off, a pun on striker as attacker.

clue.text: Not many options between Down and here

definitions.meaning: this is the third Down clue, so the Down clues before it are numbered one and two: a choice between them

explanation.surface: A small choice of routes between County Down and this spot.
explanation.walkthrough: The second definition plays on the grid: reading the Down clues up to this one, the options available are the first or the second.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase meaning a few is also literally the choice between the first two Down numbers.

clue.text: Stein's content to keep us more active

indicators.note: to keep something is to hold it within, so the beer surrounds the pronoun

parts.note: a stein is a German beer mug, so its contents are Bier, German for beer
taken as written

explanation.surface: A beer mug's contents keep us more lively.
explanation.definitionFit: Busier means occupied with more activity, a comparative synonym of more active.

clue.text: It's said to clash with band logo

indicators.note: said means spoken, so the word for the band instrument is heard, not written

parts.note: a cymbal is the percussion disc a band crashes together

explanation.surface: A band's emblem is apparently at odds with it.
explanation.definitionFit: A logo is a graphic emblem, and an emblem is a symbol standing for a company or group.

clue.text: Scoop: "Heads in shock horror love orgy!"

indicators.note: heads are the leading letters of the words that follow
an orgy is a wild, disorderly affair, so the letters of love are thrown about

explanation.surface: A tabloid exclusive headline screams about a scandalous romp.
explanation.definitionFit: To scoop and to shovel both mean to lift up with a broad blade; a scoop is also a shovel-like tool.

clue.text: Half of July in Shetland isle? That's not fair

indicators.note: one piece is placed in another, the island wrapping the month fragment

parts.note: Unst is the most northerly inhabited island of Shetland

indicators.note: half of a four-letter word is its first two letters

explanation.surface: Someone complains that summer weather in the far north is unfair.
explanation.walkthrough: UNST is the northernmost of Scotland's Shetland Islands.
explanation.definitionFit: Unjust means unfair, lacking justice; both are adjectives for unequal treatment.

clue.text: Central bank takes over society held in trust, disregarding form?

indicators.note: to take over is to replace an incumbent, so the middle letters displace the society letter

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: central letters are the middle ones of the next word

explanation.surface: The central bank seizes control of a society held in a financial trust, ignoring procedure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Form' looks like formality or paperwork; here it is a school class, which a truant skips.
explanation.definitionFit: A truant stays away from school without permission, so they ignore their class or form; the question mark flags the pun.

clue.text: Anniversary band flouts Beijing rule

indicators.note: to flout a rule is to defy it, so the letters are not kept in order

explanation.surface: A celebratory group defies China's government.
explanation.definitionFit: A jubilee is a special anniversary, and a ring marking one is a band of metal.

clue.text: Haitian settler brought back narcotic (ecstasy) stuffed in duck

indicators.note: something stuffed in goes inside, so the round letter is pushed into the others
brought back means reversed, read from right to left

parts.note: a narcotic is a drug
a duck in cricket is a score of nothing, written as O
E is slang for the drug ecstasy

explanation.surface: A Haitian colonist returns drugs stuffed inside a duck.
explanation.walkthrough: A 'settler' is not a colonist but something that settles a bill: money.
explanation.definitionFit: The gourde is the currency of Haiti, and money is what settles debts.

clue.text: Devoted to his wife, cook Roux's secured debt

indicators.note: secured means held fast, so the rearranged chef's name holds the debt note
to cook figures is to doctor them, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: an IOU is a written acknowledgment of a debt

explanation.surface: A man devoted to his spouse cooks while a famous chef's restaurant pays off a loan.
explanation.walkthrough: Roux is a famous family of French chefs in Britain, so 'cook' sits naturally with the name.
explanation.definitionFit: Uxorious describes a husband excessively fond of his wife, from the Latin for wife.

clue.text: Irish family group's penny-pinching

indicators.note: pinching means squeezing something between, so the coin is held inside the group

parts.note: a set is a group; the apostrophe s is 'has'

explanation.surface: A clan is notorious for being stingy.
explanation.definitionFit: A sept is a clan or branch of a family, especially in Ireland or Scotland.

clue.text: Making whoopee time in French king's new reign

indicators.note: one piece is put in another, the time letter inside the king's new reign

parts.note: roi is French for king, plus the possessive S

indicators.note: new signals a fresh arrangement of the letters of reign

explanation.surface: Celebrating as a French monarch begins a new reign.
explanation.definitionFit: Roistering means revelling noisily, and making whoopee is slang for wild celebration.

clue.text: Sandwich one of them in bent croquet pins

indicators.note: bent means twisted out of shape, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A snack is stuck between twisted croquet hoops.
explanation.walkthrough: Sandwich is not food here but a town in Kent, one of the Cinque Ports, an old group of English Channel harbour towns.
explanation.definitionFit: The group of medieval English coastal towns includes Sandwich, Dover, Hastings, Hythe and Romney.

clue.text: Lining up: Crucible's essential skill, they say

indicators.note: what they say is heard, so the word for the snooker skill is spoken

parts.note: the Crucible Theatre in Sheffield hosts the world snooker championship, where cueing is the key skill

explanation.surface: The setter claims standing in line is his vital talent.
explanation.walkthrough: Crucible is the setter's name, but also the Sheffield theatre that hosts snooker's world championship, where players strike the ball with a cue.
explanation.definitionFit: Queueing means standing in a line and waiting one's turn.

clue.text: Note is not deciphered by 1750?

parts.note: te is a note of the sol-fa scale

indicators.note: deciphering means working out a code, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: X as in multiplication, read as 'by'

explanation.surface: A note is not decoded by an eighteenth-century year.
explanation.walkthrough: 1750 looks like a year, but it is a time on the 24-hour clock.
explanation.definitionFit: On a 24-hour clock 17:50 is ten minutes before six in the evening.

clue.text: Aujourd'hui, trente consomment un aphrodisiaque

indicators.note: French for consume: the two French words take in the answer within their letters

explanation.surface: In French: today, thirty people consume an aphrodisiac.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is French. The answer is the French word for oyster, a famous supposed aphrodisiac; the theme hides French numbers.
explanation.definitionFit: Oysters are traditionally said to be aphrodisiac, so in French one is un aphrodisiaque.

clue.text: British family's captivated by 11 beachwear

indicators.note: captivated by means held captive inside, so the British family sits within the numbers

parts.note: eleven is written as two ones, II
kin means family; the apostrophe s is 'is'

explanation.surface: A British family is entranced by a swimsuit.
explanation.definitionFit: A bikini is a two-piece swimsuit worn on the beach.

clue.text: Battle in which fashionista Mary ceded name on her underwear

indicators.note: to cede is to give up, so the name letter is dropped

parts.note: Mary Quant was a British fashion designer associated with the miniskirt
re means on or about
bras are women's underwear

explanation.surface: A fashion designer gave up her name to a brand of lingerie.
explanation.walkthrough: Mary Quant was a 1960s London fashion designer.
explanation.definitionFit: Quatre Bras was a battle of 1815 fought two days before Waterloo.

clue.text: Come and cuff American

definitions.meaning: the folded-up hem of a trouser leg, which Americans call a cuff

explanation.definitionFit: To turn up is to arrive, and a turn-up is the British name for the American trouser cuff.

clue.text: What, at the start, some people like inhaling very strongly?

definitions.text: What, at the start, some people like inhaling very strongly?

indicators.note: the starts of the next four words give their opening letters

parts.note: ff, fortissimo, is the musical marking for very loud

explanation.surface: A question about what some people like to draw in deeply.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue defines the answer: a cannabis joint, which some like to inhale strongly.
explanation.definitionFit: A spliff is a cannabis cigarette, a joint drawn in deeply by its smoker.

clue.text: Artist's not concerned with black

indicators.note: not means without, so the letters for concerned with are taken away

parts.note: Renoir was a French Impressionist painter; the apostrophe s is 'is'
re means concerning or about

explanation.surface: A painter has no interest in the colour black.
explanation.definitionFit: Noir is French for black, used in English for dark film genres and the roulette colour.

clue.text: Caviar producer's stumped by egg

parts.note: st is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for stumped
to egg on is to urge on

explanation.surface: A caviar maker is baffled by an egg.
explanation.definitionFit: Caviar is the roe of the sturgeon, a large fish.

clue.text: Joint without approved chance to participate

indicators.note: without in the old sense of outside, so the joint goes around the approval

parts.note: a loin is a joint of meat
OK means approved

explanation.surface: A piece of meat without approval has a chance to take part.
explanation.definitionFit: A look-in is an opportunity to take part, often used in the negative: not get a look-in.

clue.text: Horsey writer's impressed by Queen galloping

indicators.note: impressed means pressed into, so the writer goes inside
galloping suggests rushing about wildly, so the letters are scrambled

parts.note: I, the person writing; the apostrophe s is 'is'

explanation.surface: A horse-loving writer is struck by the Queen riding at full gallop.
explanation.definitionFit: Equine means relating to horses, a formal synonym of horsey.

clue.text: Boffins stripped crack weapon for shooting gallery

indicators.note: to crack something is to break into it, so the stripped letters break into the weapon

parts.note: an Uzi is an Israeli submachine gun

indicators.note: stripped means peeled down, so the outer letters of Boffins are removed

explanation.surface: Scientists stripped a crack weapon for use in a shooting gallery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shooting gallery' looks like one phrase; the gallery is the Uffizi in Florence. 'stripped' takes BO and NS off Boffins to leave FFI.
explanation.definitionFit: The Uffizi in Florence is one of the world's great art galleries.
